about: Every item the optical-disc archive tracks. hosting=copy: we keep a verbatim copy (license permits it); hosting=link: we only link to it and ask the Wayback Machine to snapshot it. tools/archive.py checks, mirrors and renders this file.

categories.title: Talking to drives
categories.about: The command sets software sends to CD, DVD and Blu-ray drives over SCSI, ATAPI, SATA and USB. MMC is the standard; the Mt. Fuji specification is the industry document it grew out of.

categories.title: File systems on discs
categories.about: How files are laid out on a disc: ISO 9660 (with Joliet and Rock Ridge extensions) and UDF.

categories.title: Physical disc formats
categories.about: What the disc itself is: track geometry, modulation, error correction and recording layers for CD, DVD and their recordable kinds.

categories.title: How long discs last
categories.about: Test methods for estimating the life of recorded discs, and procedures for migrating data before they fail.

categories.title: Care, storage and handling
categories.about: How to store, handle, label and clean discs so they last, written for libraries and archives but useful to anyone with a shelf of backups.

categories.title: Open-source burning software and drivers
categories.about: Working code that drives real burners, kept with its licenses. These are the best practical documentation of how drives actually behave.

categories.title: Operating-system interfaces
categories.about: How each operating system lets programs reach a drive, and the official documentation for it.

categories.title: Community databases
categories.about: Shared records that make reading and copying discs reliable: drive read offsets, verified dumps of pressed discs, and the identifiers that look up a CD's tracks.

categories.title: Who still makes drives and discs
categories.about: Dated news about manufacturers leaving or staying in the market. Useful for judging how long blanks and drives will be easy to buy.

categories.title: Licensed and paid specifications
categories.about: Specifications that can only be bought or licensed. We record what they are and where to get them, and keep no copies.

items.title: Blu-ray Disc specifications
Stability comparison of recordable optical discs: a study of error rates in harsh conditions (J. Res. NIST 109, 517, 2004)
items.license: Public domain: a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. § 105).
items.notes: Accelerated ageing of CD-R and DVD±R under heat, humidity and light. Good discs proved very stable, but stability differed widely between manufacturers, and light exposure measurably raised error rates.

items.title: NIST SP 500-263: NIST/Library of Congress optical media longevity study, test procedure (2005)
items.license: Public domain: a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. § 105).
items.notes: The procedure, based on ISO 18927, for estimating the life expectancy of CD-ROM, DVD-ROM, CD-R, DVD±R and DVD±RW, plus a shelf-life test of blank media.

items.title: NIST/Library of Congress optical disc longevity study: final report
items.publisher: NIST and Library of Congress (Zheng, Slattery)
items.license: Public domain: a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. § 105).
items.notes: Life-expectancy estimates for recordable CDs and DVDs. The Library summarised that CDs tended to outlast DVDs, and that the discs are only as durable as the drives left to read them.

items.title: Longevity of CD media: research at the Library of Congress
items.license: Public domain: a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. § 105).
items.notes: Natural and accelerated ageing of the Library's pressed audio CDs and CD-ROMs, including the effect of adhesive labels.

items.title: CCI Notes 19/1: Longevity of recordable CDs, DVDs and Blu-rays (revised 2019)
items.notes: The most recent government summary covering BD-R as well as CD-R and DVD±R. Iraci's earlier CCI work found DVD±RW and dual-layer DVDs fair to very poor for long-term use, while DVD±R with a gold metal layer held up well and silver-layer discs degraded quickly.

items.title: CD formats and their longevity: FAQ
items.publisher: Canadian Conservation Institute and Library and Archives Canada

items.title: Longevity of optical disc media: accelerated ageing predictions and natural ageing data (Restaurator, 2017)
items.notes: Compares Arrhenius predictions with discs that aged naturally: the method held for CD-R, but its very long predictions for recordable DVDs were not borne out.

items.title: M-DISC: summary of the U.S. Navy (NAWCWD China Lake) longevity test
items.notes: A manufacturer's one-page summary of a Navy test comparing M-DISC DVD with dye-based DVDs, reporting no data degradation on the M-DISC samples. Treat it as a vendor document; the full report is not publicly posted.
